claims.text: localStorage stores string values by key (getItem/setItem/removeItem), one store per web address (origin: scheme, host, port); a value written is read back as a string.
claims.source_hint: HTML Standard, Web storage: the Storage interface; the localStorage getter (storage per origin)

claims.text: Values in localStorage survive a page reload and closing the tab (unlike sessionStorage), until the site's code or the user removes them.
claims.source_hint: HTML Standard, Web storage: introduction (localStorage spans multiple windows and lasts beyond the current session)

claims.text: The browser limits how much one web address (origin) may keep in localStorage; the amount is set by the browser, not by the page.
claims.source_hint: HTML Standard, Web storage: user agents should limit the total amount of space allowed for storage areas; Storage quota

claims.text: At stage-2, productsProvider is a FutureProvider that only calls fetchProducts; the screen's error builder shows 'Could not load products.' (after Riverpod's default retries), and nothing is saved on the device.

Stage-3 productsProvider: reads the saved list, yields it if present, calls fetchProducts, writes the fresh list as JSON under savedProductsKey ('donhang.products') and yields it; on Exception rethrows if nothing saved, else yields the saved list with outOfDate: true.

A Riverpod StreamProvider whose body is an async* function exposes each yielded value to watchers as AsyncValue data; a ConsumerWidget watching it is marked to rebuild before the next frame (several values in one frame give one build).

Riverpod 3.0 by default retries a provider whose computation throws, several times with a wait between; a retry function returning null disables it. Here, in the load, only the rethrow (nothing saved) fails the provider; the caught on Exception path is never retried.
claims.source_hint: riverpod.dev/docs: Automatic retry (retry parameter, returning null stops retrying); stage-2/3 providers.dart retry comment

claims.text: Because the write comes after a successful fetchProducts, a failed load never overwrites the saved copy; readSavedProducts returns null when the key is missing and decodes the JSON otherwise.

apiClientProvider gives the API client, as at stage-2; localStoreProvider (lib/offline/local_store.dart) gives the browser's localStorage on the web and an in-memory MemoryLocalStore elsewhere; tests override it.

Stage-3 screen: loading → const LoadingView(); error → MessageView(productsLoadError); data → Column with a warning StatusBanner(savedListBanner) when loaded.outOfDate, above the catalog. English banner: 'Showing the saved list: the API did not answer, so it may be out of date.'
localStorage holds only what code writes into it, not the app's files: a reload must fetch the web bundle from the network or the browser's HTTP cache before Dart code can read it.
